name: Katazome and Ise katagami stencil print
summary: A stencil is cut in layers of mulberry paper, and rice-paste resist is spread through it onto cloth. The cloth is then dyed. The result is a repeat pattern with sharp white edges and flat colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: A pattern cut once in paper can be printed a thousand times as a sharp white shape on dyed cloth, if the stencil holds its islands with thin bridges.
design_principles: Cut the pattern in 2–3 layers of washi that are pasted with persimmon tannin (kakishibu), so the stencil stays stiff and wet-proof.
Keep each cut line 0.1–0.5 mm wide, and keep at least 0.5 mm of paper between two cuts.
Hold each free island of paper with a thin bridge, a tie bar, or with a net of silk thread between the layers.
Spread the rice-paste resist through the stencil in one pass of a spatula, and let it dry before you dye.
Dye the cloth after the resist dries. The resist stays white, and the dye fills the rest as a flat colour.
Repeat the pattern on the cloth, and join each repeat so the seam does not show.
Choose a small, fine motif: a wave, a plant, a crest, a bird. Allow a pictorial scene only in mingei work.
anti_patterns: A soft gradient or a tonal shade
A woodgrain texture or a thick outline
A pattern whose islands float with no bridge

process.matrix: A stencil (katagami) of 2–3 layers of mulberry washi, pasted with persimmon tannin and cut with fine knives. A net of silk thread can hold the islands.
process.press: No press. A worker spreads rice-paste resist through the stencil with a spatula, then brushes or dips the cloth in dye.
process.image_making: A cutter, a specialist of Shiroko and Jike in Ise, cuts the pattern. A dyer uses the stencil many times.
process.edition: Many metres of repeat pattern. The same stencil serves for years.

inks.strategy: Plant dye on cloth: indigo for the ground, with persimmon brown and madder red as accents. The resist leaves the pattern in the cloth colour.

screening.rule: Make each area a flat dye or a flat resist white. The pattern shows a tone only by the density of its small cuts.

registration.rule: Fit each repeat of the stencil to the last one within 0.3 mm, with the pins or the marks on the cloth.

substrate.stock: Cotton or silk cloth, undyed before the dye bath.
substrate.finish: Plain weave, washed free of size, so the dye takes evenly.

surface.impression: None. The paste leaves a thin skin that the wash removes.
surface.sheen: Matt, with the soft shine of silk or the dry look of cotton.
surface.texture: Sharp white edges on a flat dye, a visible weave of the cloth, and a fine repeat.

marks: bridges and tie bars in the stencil
fibre and weave of the cloth
slight leak of dye at a thin cut

emotion.target_response: Clear, quiet order: the viewer feels a fine pattern that stays sharp, and a craft that repeats with calm care.

avoid_when: The picture needs gradation, a photograph or a painted tone.
The brief needs a rough, hand-cut block look.

modifiers.how: Use one stencil for each colour on paper, apply gouache with a dabbing brush, and add a printed key line.
Replace the repeat by a single scene, print on washi, and use wiped colour with a sumi key line.
